findings: Small local gate with a single sha2 dependency and no runtime service abstraction; it checks file bytes directly and fails with concrete diagnostics.
Moves Cloud IaC from catalog-only skeleton rows toward supply-chain-shaped local provenance while refusing to overclaim signing, SLSA, provider locks, registry APIs, or plan/apply.
Tests and live gate cover unknown lane RED, digest drift, missing required digest, manifest scope drift, catalog/provenance key matching, path containment, and skeleton overclaim guards.
Command has live repo defaults and reports manifest/catalog/provenance paths plus module/file counts.

Focused tests, live gate, Cloud IaC regressions, scoped check/clippy/fmt, JSON/audit parsing, planning/api/architecture gates, honest/retired vocabulary, run-all 86/86, and strict dependency-seam are recorded.
Rejected fake signing/SLSA/provider-lock claims; chose local SHA-256 source provenance as the smallest honest next gate before provider-lock/signature slices.
Gate canonicalizes paths, rejects absolute/parent traversal for repo-relative paths, requires digest matches current bytes, and records that no secrets/provider credentials are used.
Bounded local filesystem scan of 12 small files; no provider calls, network, or runtime hot path.
Explicit non-claims distinguish local source digests from SLSA attestation, provider lock/provenance, deployment, SLO, DR, or hyperscaler readiness evidence.
Existing module-catalog, GitOps evidence, cell-topology, and OpenTofu validation gates remain green; run-all aggregate now passes 86/86.
